channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc.
item.description: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company, folding Pierre's Trees and Diffs libraries—already used by Codex—and its Code Storage feature into Codex while keeping them open source. (OpenAI News)

item.title: BYOK and enterprise custom models in the Copilot usage API
item.description: The Copilot usage metrics API separates BYOK across GitHub Copilot from Copilot-hosted model usage, covering local BYOK via Ollama, Foundry Local, LM Studio and llama-server, with enterprise and organization reports at user and aggregate levels for 1-day and 28-day windows. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
item.description: StateBench tests long-context state tracking across four difficulty levels and finds recurrent and hybrid models generalize farther than transformers, while frontier models fail on harder tasks and longer inputs. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Daybreak Red is now available in AWS GovCloud (US-East)
item.description: Daybreak Red now offers GPT-5.6 Cyber to approved government security teams in AWS GovCloud (US-East) via Amazon Bedrock for vulnerability research, reproduction and remediation assessment, with inference data excluded from model training. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
item.description: In a real lung cancer case, Google Antigravity with Cheminformatics Skills let an agent search thousands of compounds, run matched molecular pair analysis, and propose novel rigidified macrocycles and synthesis routes within an hour, versus days for typical iteration. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
item.description: IBM Research's Palette fine-tunes a 20B model with LoRA, splits deck-building into designer planning and coder page-by-page code, speeds the coding stage about 6–7x, and ranks first in two of three PresentBench domains. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Dependabot version updates support Agent Package Manager
item.description: Dependabot version updates now support Agent Package Manager, opening pull requests for git dependencies declared in apm.yml, regenerating apm.lock.yaml, and covering version rather than security updates on all GitHub plans, with GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24 support coming. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: OpenAI employees' side-hustle hardware: GPT-6 Astra goes from renders in a week to samples in a month
item.description: Two OpenAI employees used GPT-6 Astra to design a Codex-interacting test device in under a week, and a contract manufacturer delivered a prototype in under a month, though mass production still hinges on dimensional tolerances and assembly details. (AIbase)

item.title: One person, one day: the "AI copilot" mode behind Windows 11's native speed test tool
item.description: Marcus Ash says Windows 11 26H2's native speed test tool was prototyped in one day by Diego Bacca in his spare time, with an AI agent handling iteration, while an earlier Ookla collaboration was just a Bing web wrapper. (AIbase)

item.title: ByteDance Tightens Internal AI Access: Reported Company-Wide Ban on External AI for L4 Code Repos, Executive Stresses Balancing Confidentiality and Usability
item.description: ByteDance reportedly blocks external AI tools from its company-wide L4 code repositories and Feishu documents, with self-funded Claude and Codex accounts disabled in core areas as VP Hong Dingkun warns L3-plus leaks carry severe consequences. (AIbase)

item.title: How far are robots from autonomously completing complex tasks? Wang Xingxing on breakthrough directions for embodied intelligence
item.description: Unitree Robotics founder Wang Xingxing says embodied AI must solve the last few millimeters of physical alignment and touch in assembly/disassembly, targeting voice-driven completion of 80% of tasks in 80% of unfamiliar scenes, with 2027 possibly the generalization turning point. (AIbase)

item.title: 灵光开放生态持续扩容，新增微信读书、夸克、哈啰打车、麦当劳等多项服务连接
item.description: On November 4, Ant Lingguang's upgrade added connectors such as WeChat Reading, podcast subscriptions, Quark Cloud Drive, Hello Taxi and McDonald's, expanding its open ecosystem to 40 external connections for daily scenarios. (AIbase)

item.title: Building its own chips with its own LLM: Anthropic assembles a 15-person chip design team, with Claude helping accelerate R&D
item.description: Anthropic has assembled a 15-person chip design team that uses its own Claude model to handle engineering and design work for custom chips, with internal tests claiming a significantly shorter design cycle than conventional Nvidia and AMD processes. (AIbase)

item.title: Google hasn’t figured out how to make AI pay like its search engine
item.description: Alphabet reports the fastest search-query growth in five years, yet Q3 Search revenue growth slowed from about 17% to 12% and paid clicks from 13% to 8%, with AI Mode monetizing below traditional search. (The Verge)

item.title: Orphex MCP — Run your entire digital marketing stack via one unified MCP
item.description: Orphex MCP's title claims one unified MCP can run an entire digital marketing stack, but the body is only a CAPTCHA security verification screen, leaving no substantive content to read. (Product Hunt)

item.title: Baidu unveils Apollo World, its first physical AI world model, with nearly 100 Apollo Go robotaxis now running on the new architecture
item.description: Baidu unveiled Apollo World, its first physical-AI world model, in Shenzhen on November 3, as Wang Liang said about 100 Apollo Go robotaxis run on a next-generation end-to-end architecture with nearly 1 million fully driverless safety kilometers. (AIbase)
